latest_holdout.note: Separate from the repeated 160-game development seed, but this 400-game validation seed was also used for the frozen control and intermediate city-reply variant. Not a new human match or a formal evaluation.

human_review.scope: Eight main-site v7 losses and three earlier QueueT losses, using only the recorded player observations. Isolated v8 probes are not matches or human-strength evidence.
human_review.probe_scope: Only recorded own legal observations enter the controllers. New decisions are not executed; subsequent frames remain historical. No alternate win result is asserted. Debug values are copied before observation expiry, and the underlying source identity was verified.

findings.observed: At 1312 the enemy city held 490 after merging a 377-troop column; home was sixteen steps away. At the loss our total was still 1003 versus 746, but home had only 189 versus the adjacent 345.
findings.implication: Count force deliverable along actual routes before the arrival deadline; total army is not available defense.
findings.addressed: Longer mobilization deadlines, without a permanent long-range static garrison.

findings.observed: At 810 enemy 33 was beside city 228 with 147; at 811 that city had 179, and at 812 the 179-troop column sortied. Our historical 85-troop landing could be intercepted in one order.
findings.implication: A productive city is a reinforcement and sortie point. Evaluate active visible replies, including a source hit and destination reinforcement.
findings.addressed: Common visible one-order interception check. Exact Arena seat order applies locally; recorded online outcomes are not assumed to have the same ordering.

findings.observed: At 372 a 75-troop column bought a 47-troop neutral city. The 87-troop attacker first became visible at 373. Both local cities were subsequently lost.
findings.implication: A purchase must leave an affordable occupation and supporting column; the unseen later attacker cannot be inserted into the earlier observation.
findings.addressed: Post-program city security using one conserved troop ledger and a public-army prior, not hidden positions.

findings.observed: City 151 was captured at 271, lost at 283, captured at 292 and lost at 302. Enemy city 183 remained its production and assembly base.
findings.implication: A capture is not a durable occupation. Reinforcement, a field defender and future sorties need a continuing shared action schedule.
findings.addressed: Partially addressed. Persistent occupation and a complete campaign controller remain unresolved.

findings.observed: The first raid exposed the home neighbourhood at 150. We withdrew repeatedly afterward. A second 62-troop column appeared at 178 against a 13-troop home.
findings.implication: The opponent retains knowledge of the exposed general after its scout leaves. A fresh raid is not a fresh information state.
findings.addressed: Post-raid rebuilding is improved; permanent exposure-aware strategy remains unresolved. Scouting intent is inferred from the observed sequence.

command_and_occupation_followup.status: Provisional behavior corrections; no demonstrated strength gain or human-level result.

paired_ffa.interpretation: Same four-player pool and eighty scheduled games: 35 to 38 wins, mean rank 2.100 to 2.025. A small observed change, not sufficient evidence of general superiority or human-level strength.

human_full_history_probe.scope: Recorded own legal observation streams. Alternative actions are NOT executed; later frames remain historical. This is no evidence of alternate wins. Diagnostics copy values inside arena_act before observation expiry. Instrumented-source timing is separate from the unchanged candidate Arena timing.
human_full_history_probe.timing_scope: Instrumented diagnostic only; excluded from the unmodified candidate Arena timing.

action_economy.scope: Historical own legal observations and submitted actions only. Attempts are not guaranteed executed orders; short ownership duration is descriptive, not proof that the move was bad. New-vision updates are not attributed causally to a particular action.
action_economy.counting_note: Losses and recaptures count events/attempts, not distinct squares. Submitted online instructions can be repeated or unexecuted; no causal win claim is made from these counts.

profiling.scope: First twelve games, not a representative all-map timing guarantee. All fourteen optional stages were entered in the control sample; that sample does not support blanket attribution of stagnation to the planning clock.

behavior_comparison.scope: First eighty matched-seed historical games, descriptive rather than causal.

remaining_findings: In the continuous historical probe, the candidate still leaves some newly captured cities. In game 6, the 48-troop enemy first becomes visible at tick 340, after the tick-338 exit. Merely keeping the 33-troop garrison would not defeat it. A supported occupation, withdrawal and reassembly plan remains unresolved.

In game 9 after tick 150, 223 of 523 submitted attacks on non-owned squares aimed at ordinary land lost within the previous 30 ticks. 112 used a source with at least 30 troops. These are attempts, not confirmed executed actions, and recapture is not automatically a mistake. The current fixed ordinary-land reward should be audited against actual holding time and transport/vision value.

The candidate preserves the front army before the previously unseen counterattack and starts earlier reinforcement against the recorded distant column, in continuous historical probes. Later frames are the original game, so neither result proves a saved game.

Human sequences show reusable field columns returning through productive cities, source/landing interceptions, and repeat raids after reconnaissance. Independent task prizes do not yet guarantee a shared campaign schedule that retains a mobile defender, explores a different route, and delivers reinforcement on time.

paired_reconnaissance_comparison.note: The observed win difference is inconclusive; do not treat the development score of 73.75% as stable strength.

discovery_diagnostic.scope: First 80 games of the paired validation; only each player legal observation is inspected.

paired_capital_comparison.note: The per-game McNemar number is unadjusted for map rotation clustering; the direct observed change is 254 to 289 wins on the same 400 scheduled games. The 80% target is not met.

paired_interception_comparison.note: The per-game McNemar number is unadjusted for map rotation clustering. The direct observed change is 289 to 281 wins on the same 400 scheduled games; fixing recorded tactical interceptions did not establish a duel-strength improvement.

city_assembly_trial.note: Rejected as a combined change after a 115-to-106 win regression on the repeated development seed. Adding cities indiscriminately as assembly candidates is not evidence of learning effective human staging.

city_sortie_paired_trial.note: Not retained: 281 to 278 wins on the same 400 scheduled games, three changed to wins and six to losses; this does not establish a benefit. Both rejected variants remain archived.

failed_regression_experiments.failure: city sortie replaced by collection; candidate not promoted
A rear transport displaced the available city half sortie; also incurred a recorded decision timeout.

One of fourteen tests failed: the recorded unsupported neutral-city purchase was selected again. The later funded-city variant passed all fourteen. This failed run remains preserved; a separate instrumented probe chose a safe move, so timing-dependent proposal coverage is a hypothesis, not an established sole cause.
